newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FINANCE DEPT SEEKS VETO ON PROVINCIAL BUDGETS.
newsitem.headline: FINANCE DEPT SEEKS VETO ON PROVINCIAL BUDGETS.

text.p: The South African Finance Ministry on Tuesday proposed amendments to a draft law on local finance to ensure it retains control over municipal budgeting.

"The Minister (of Finance) must have the power of financial oversight and monitoring over all spheres, departments and corporations of government," Director General of Finance Maria Ramos said in a letter to the parliamentary committee on provincial affairs.
"The Minister of Finance's fiscal authority cannot be compromised or weakened if he is to exercised his function of ensuring macro-economic stability in an effective manner," she said.

The government earlier this month launched a rescue package for 95 municipalities on the brink of bankruptcy, but said those that failed to manage their finances responsibly would have to be taken over by the national administration.

Almost 10 percent of South African municipalities are in trouble as a result of poor financial management and outstanding service payments totalling 5.6 billion rand ($1.2 billion) at the end of June.
Ramos proposed that the Local Government Transition Act Second Amendment Bill currently before parliament should oblige municipalities to submit their budgets to the Finance Minister for approval.

The bill already provides for the central government to set upper limits on municipal spending and budget growth and on the application of funds, including a cap on the percentage used for personnel costs.
Ramos said the approval threshold for municipal borrowing should be raised from a simple majority to a two thirds of all members of a municipal council.

"The Minister of Finance must be notified of any intention by a municipality to raise a loan other than loans for bridging finance...at least 30 days before embarking on any negotiations for such a loan," she said.
Ramos also proposed that the Minister of Finance should have a veto power over municipal investment policies.
